industry: healthcare (outpatient physical, occupational and hand therapy)

opportunities.title: Rebuild the Spotswood front door: a real location page, correct phone routing, and machine-readable NAP for both clinics
opportunities.problem: The Spotswood clinic's Google profile points at a website that does not contain Spotswood. There is no Spotswood page in the 14-page sitemap, no Spotswood address, hours or phone anywhere on the site, the header click-to-call on every page dials the Lakewood number, and the scheduling form's Location dropdown offers only 'Lakewood' - so a Spotswood patient who does what the listing tells them to do reaches a Lakewood page and cannot even select their own clinic on the form. The same town is also split across a second, unclaimed Google listing and an unclaimed Birdeye profile.
evidence: Google Business Profile 'First Rehab Physical Therapy', 404 Main St #A, Spotswood NJ 08884 - 5.0 from 10 reviews, phone (732) 251-6640, website first-rehab.com: https://www.google.com/maps/search/First+Rehab+404+Main+St+Spotswood+NJ

Locations page publishes only the Lakewood clinic (1352 River Avenue, Unit 3) with 732.884.2020 / 732.200.0954 and the note 'Hours are subject to change. Please call to confirm.': https://first-rehab.com/locations/
Page sitemap has 14 pages and no Spotswood location page: https://first-rehab.com/page-sitemap.xml
Scheduling form Location dropdown contains only 'Lakewood': https://first-rehab.com/schedule-an-appointment/
Header click-to-call on every page is the Lakewood number 732.884.2020, next to a 'BOOK NOW' button that leads to the request form: https://first-rehab.com/
Organization JSON-LD carries only name, url, logo and a LinkedIn sameAs - no address, phone, hours, no LocalBusiness/MedicalClinic type, no Spotswood entity: https://first-rehab.com/

A second, separate Google listing exists for the town ('First Rehab Outpatient Therapy Provider Spotswood') with no reviews and no website shown: https://www.google.com/maps/search/First+Rehab+404+Main+St+Spotswood+NJ

Birdeye profile at the Spotswood address is unclaimed ('This profile has not been claimed by the business owner'), showing generic Mon-Fri 9-6 hours that match neither Google nor the site: https://reviews.birdeye.com/first-rehab-286008032

Spotswood's advertised hours (Mon/Wed/Fri 8AM-4PM, Tue/Thu 8AM-6PM, weekends closed) give roughly 44 clinical hours a week that are published only on Google, not on any page of the site: https://www.google.com/maps/search/First+Rehab+404+Main+St+Spotswood+NJ
opportunities.agent_design: Not a chat agent - this is the foundation the other agents stand on. Build one location record per clinic (address, local phone, hours, clinicians, directions, parking) as the single source of truth, generate a Spotswood page and a Spotswood-aware locations page from it, emit per-clinic LocalBusiness/MedicalClinic JSON-LD with address, telephone, openingHoursSpecification and geo, and put a plain-text 'Spotswood clinic: address / hours / phone' block on-page that assistants can quote. Route the header tel: link by which clinic page the visitor is on, add 'Spotswood' and 'Lakewood' to the Contact Form 7 location field, and add a status line the site currently lacks ('open now / closed, call back at'). A small monitoring agent then re-crawls the site, both Google listings, Birdeye and the main directories weekly and alerts when NAP or hours drift apart, and checks whether the two Google entities still both exist. The duplicate-listing claim/merge and any Google profile edits are done by the owner inside their own accounts - we prepare the changes, they approve and apply.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The gap is not one page edit; it is a single source of truth feeding a CMS page, two Google entities, an unclaimed Birdeye profile and structured data, with drift detection afterwards. A staff edit fixes the page and leaves the JSON-LD, the phone routing, the form dropdown and the duplicate listing wrong, and nothing notices when hours change again - which matters because the site already tells patients to call to confirm hours.

impact_estimate.range: No dollar figure modelled. The observable defect count today is: 1 of 2 clinics with no address, hours or phone on the site it links to from Google; 1 of 2 clinics absent from the booking form's location options; 1 duplicate Google entity and 1 unclaimed directory profile for the same address; 0 location-scoped structured data records. Post-fix the same form and page serve both clinics and one answerable hours source replaces 'please call to confirm'.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Counts are read directly from the profile URLs above, not estimated. No NJ physical-therapy front-door conversion or cost-per-acquisition benchmark exists in the industry brief, so no revenue is claimed; the inference is that some share of Spotswood searches currently lands on a Lakewood-only page and is lost or misrouted, but that share is unmeasured (Search Console and GBP insights baselines should be captured on day 1 of the pilot).

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: baseline captured from Search Console and both Google profiles; a built Spotswood location page with address, local phone (732) 251-6640, hours, directions and the treating clinicians; per-clinic JSON-LD and a plain-text NAP block; header tel: routing and the form's location field fixed; a documented duplicate-listing and Birdeye claim checklist for the owner to execute; a weekly NAP-drift monitor running. Success measure is measurable rather than rhetorical: Spotswood page indexed and served for 'First Rehab Spotswood hours', form submissions selectable by location, and zero NAP mismatches across tracked sources.

opportunities.title: Intake and eligibility agent that answers, screens and books new patients at both clinics, including after hours
opportunities.problem: Every new patient enters through a free-text request form that asks for a diagnosis and a referral source, shows no availability, and then depends on a staff callback to turn into an appointment; insurance verification is explicitly pushed to the phone; and both clinics are shut when working patients are free to call (Spotswood closed weekends and after 4-6PM, Lakewood closes 1:30PM Friday). A 2022 local feature says booking ran through a separate 24-hour call centre, and whether that coverage still exists is unconfirmed - so the front desk is carrying intake, benefit checks and the callback queue by hand.
evidence: Scheduling page is a Contact Form 7 form (Name, Diagnosis, Email, Phone, Location, Referral source) behind reCAPTCHA v3, with no slots shown - a staff member calls back to schedule: https://first-rehab.com/schedule-an-appointment/
FAQ routes insurance verification to a phone call: 'Please call us at 732.884.2020, and we will gladly verify your insurance benefits': https://first-rehab.com/faqs/

FAQ also states the intake reality: treatment is typically 2-3 visits a week for 4-8 weeks, ~1-hour sessions, 'We work with Medicare and most insurance providers', and evaluation notes are sent to the referring physician: https://first-rehab.com/faqs/

Spotswood hours leave the clinic unreachable for much of a working day and all weekend: Mon/Wed/Fri 8AM-4PM, Tue/Thu 8AM-6PM, Sat/Sun closed: https://www.google.com/maps/search/First+Rehab+404+Main+St+Spotswood+NJ
Lakewood hours run to 1:30PM on Friday and the site itself says 'Hours are subject to change. Please call to confirm.': https://first-rehab.com/locations/

Paperwork is still completed on paper on arrival 15 minutes early, and follow-up appointments are arranged in person by the scheduling team before the patient leaves: https://first-rehab.com/new-patients/
A separate 24-hour call centre number (732-370-2010) handled bookings in 2022; current after-hours coverage is unverified: https://thevoiceoflakewood.com/first-rehab/
Tech stack is WordPress plus Contact Form 7 and reCAPTCHA only - no booking engine, patient portal or live chat anywhere on the site: https://first-rehab.com/

The clerical task set being automated is documented occupationally - scheduling appointments, completing insurance forms and maintaining records (Dental Assistants, SOC 31-9091): https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/31-9091.00
opportunities.agent_design: Two intake surfaces over one agent. (1) Web: the form becomes an agent conversation that collects name, contact, referral source, body region/reason for visit, preferred clinic (Lakewood or Spotswood, finally reachable), insurance plan and member ID, and preferred times - then reads real availability and offers slots. (2) Phone: a voice/SMS agent answers calls the clinic misses, including nights and weekends, with a hard rule set: it never gives clinical advice, it screens for red flags (post-surgical complications, suspected fracture, chest pain, neuro deficit) and hands those straight to a human, and it escalates workers' compensation, attorney/liens, out-of-network and self-pay cases to the front desk rather than booking. Benefit checks run as eligibility transactions through the practice's clearinghouse rather than free text, so results conform to standard code sets; if the clearinghouse integration is not in place at pilot start, the agent collects the details, drafts the verification request and a staff member approves the result. Systems touched: website form, telephony/messaging, the practice-management calendar (write access), the clearinghouse. Human approval sits on every exception class, on red-flag calls, and on any benefit estimate quoted to a patient. All of it runs under a BAA, with PHI minimisation, role-based access and audit logging; no clinical recommendation is generated by the agent.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This writes to a scheduling system, transacts eligibility against a payer/clearinghouse, spans two sites with different hours and phone numbers, and must refuse to behave like a triage nurse. A chatbot subscription can collect a name and an email; it cannot see the calendar, cannot run an eligibility check, will not hold a HIPAA-compliant audit trail, and would happily answer a clinical question it must never answer.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $200-$750/month in front-desk handling time across the two clinics (about $2,400-$9,000/year), plus unbounded upside from after-hours inquiries that currently reach no one, which is not counted because the call volume is unknown.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 10-15 minutes of front-desk work per new patient for the callback loop and benefit check (an inference: scheduling, insurance forms and record-keeping are the documented clerical task set at https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/31-9091.00, and the FAQ routes verification to a phone call), priced at the New Jersey Dental Assistant median of $22.50/hr from the industry brief as the nearest clerical benchmark collected - no NJ receptionist or medical-secretary wage was obtained, so this is a proxy - with ~30% payroll burden, i.e. about $29/hr. Assumes 40-100 new patients a month across both clinics; the practice publishes no volume figures. No time-and-motion measurement exists for PT intake, so the range is deliberately wide and low.

opportunities.pilot_scope: First 2-4 weeks deliberately staged without voice: web and SMS/email intake agent live for both locations, writing real slots to the calendar for one visit type, with eligibility handled as a staff-approved draft; red-flag and payer-exception routing tested against a scripted set of ~30 scenarios the clinical director signs off; a logging and BAA review before any PHI flows. Deliverable is measured on: share of new-patient requests that reach a booked slot without a callback, average time from request to confirmed appointment, and zero clinical advice given.

opportunities.title: Continuity agent for a 2-3x/week course of care: reminders, conversational reschedules across both sites, discharge recall and review requests
opportunities.problem: The practice's own FAQ says each patient is typically in 2-3 times a week for 4-8 weeks, so a single missed hour is a lost therapist-hour in a schedule with no slack - and nothing on the site or in the tech stack shows any reminder, reschedule or recall messaging. Hours shift and the site tells patients to call to confirm, which pushes last-minute changes onto the phone. Meanwhile visible social proof is stale: Google reviews are roughly 4-7 years old and the Birdeye profile is unclaimed, so no automated review request is running either.
evidence: Treatment frequency and course length: 'typically 2-3 visits a week for 4-8 weeks', ~1-hour sessions: https://first-rehab.com/faqs/

No booking engine, patient portal, messaging platform or live chat on the site - static pages plus two forms only, and the Birdeye profile is unclaimed so no reputation-automation vendor is in place: https://reviews.birdeye.com/first-rehab-286008032
Visible Google reviews on the Spotswood profile are roughly 4-7 years old with nothing recent; 5.0 from 10 reviews: https://www.google.com/maps/search/First+Rehab+404+Main+St+Spotswood+NJ
Site states hours are 'subject to change. Please call to confirm.', making the clinic the only source of truth on the day: https://first-rehab.com/locations/
Two clinics with different hours and separate numbers means a reschedule has to know which site the patient is booked at: https://www.google.com/maps/search/First+Rehab+404+Main+St+Spotswood+NJ

Peer-reviewed evidence that reminder modality matters: a rapid systematic review of predictive-model-based no-show interventions found model-driven text reminders reduced no-shows (median RR 0.91, high certainty), phone-call reminders median RR 0.61 across 3 RCTs, and patient navigators RR 0.55 (95% CI 0.46-0.67): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36508503/

Pilot RCT (720 patients who had no-showed): up to three text messages raised completed rescheduled visits by 2.83 percentage points (95% CI 1.66-4.00; OR 1.86), while the effect on merely rescheduling was not significant: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38852906/
Wage benchmark: New Jersey physical therapist median $50.00/hr, mean annual $109,280 (May 2023): https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes_nj.htm
opportunities.agent_design: Event-driven off the practice-management schedule, no new system of record. Triggers: T-72h and T-24h reminders carrying the clinic address, the local phone number and parking/arrival note (fixing the 'call to confirm hours' problem at the moment it matters); free-text replies interpreted conversationally - a patient who says 'I can't make Thursday' gets two or three real alternative slots, first at their own clinic and then at the other one if the drive is shorter, and the agent writes the change back so the freed hour is immediately re-offerable to a waitlist; no-reply or repeated-miss escalation to the front desk with context, not a raw list of names. A separate arm handles continuity: a patient who has not been seen for two weeks inside an active plan of care gets a check-in and a booking link; a discharged patient gets one review request pointing at the correct Google profile (Spotswood or Lakewood); a lapsed patient at 6-8 weeks gets a recall message. The agent never discusses symptoms, never advises on exercise progression and never contacts a patient about clinical findings - any clinical reply is handed to the treating therapist. Human approval sits on all clinical escalations, on complaints, and on any message template change; all PHI-minimised and sent through a BAA-covered messaging vendor.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The cheap version - a reminder-text subscription bolted to a calendar - cannot read a reply and rebook, cannot offer a slot at the other clinic, cannot write the freed hour back into the schedule for the waitlist, and cannot tell which of two Google profiles a discharged patient should be pointed at. The value is in the write-back and the two-site routing, which is integration work, not messaging.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $80-$850/month across both clinics (about $1,000-$10,000/year) in recovered therapist-hours, from cutting missed visits by 9-39% on an assumed 2-5 missed visits per clinic per week.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 2-5 missed or late-cancelled 1-hour visits per clinic per week - the practice publishes no no-show rate and no public reviews mention waits or no-shows, so this is an assumption, not a measurement, and it is the main uncertainty. Reduction band taken from the review's median relative effects: 9% for text reminders (high certainty) up to 39% for staff phone calls (moderate certainty, i.e. the ceiling if the agent reaches a human-equivalent contact rate). Each recovered hour valued at the NJ physical therapist median of $50.00/hr from the industry brief, which credits the therapist-hour rather than net revenue - no billed-charge or collection-rate data was available, so this understates cash value and overstates it if the hour is not backfillable. Reschedule recovery (the +2.83pp completed-rescheduled-visits pilot) and any review-driven new-patient effect are excluded from the range because they are not measured for this practice.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks at one clinic (Spotswood, the smaller and better-instrumented of the two): reminders with two-way reply handling, a live waitlist that receives freed hours, cross-clinic slot offers, and a discharge review request to the correct Google profile. Baseline and exit measured on missed-visit rate, share of cancellations self-rescheduled without staff contact, hours recovered by the waitlist, and review count on the Spotswood profile. The clinical director approves all message copy before send and sees every escalation.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (24/30): the front-door and intake gaps are verified on the live site, the sitemap, the Contact Form 7 form and three separate directory profiles - a two-clinic practice whose website contains one clinic and whose booking form cannot accept the other. That is unusually concrete. The continuity opportunity is weaker: no review or public record shows a no-show problem, so it rests on the FAQ's 2-3 visits-a-week cadence and is scored as inference. Fit (16/20): these are capabilities G and A - front door, intake, scheduling, benefit verification and follow-up - which are the core of what we build. There is no physical/edge component here and no avenues.json was supplied, so no E opportunity is proposed; the only sensor-ish asset would be the gym floor, and the evidence does not support pushing hardware into a small PT clinic. Ability to pay (13/20): two locations, six named clinicians, insurance billing, a 2021 acquisition by The Towne Group and $50/hr NJ PT labour all point to a real P&L, but it is a small practice, the visible decision-maker is a clinical director rather than an owner, and ownership sits with a group whose budget authority is unverified. Ease (11/15): the front-door work is days not months and the fixes are provable to the owner in one page; the intake agent is a genuine integration project with HIPAA and calendar-write risk, which slows the second and third sale. Strategic (12/15): the multi-site-PT pattern - listing exists, site ignores half the footprint, request-only form, phone-only benefit checks - is extremely common among independent NJ therapy clinics, so the first build is reusable; healthcare raises the compliance bar and lowers reuse speed slightly. Evidence is not thin overall, but one of the three opportunities is inference-led and the dollar figures are modest and assumption-driven - this is a well-evidenced small account, not a large one.

best_evidence_signal: First Rehab's Spotswood Google profile (5.0 from 10 reviews) links to first-rehab.com, where the sitemap, locations page and the booking form's location dropdown offer only Lakewood - the clinic's own site never publishes its Spotswood address, hours, phone or a way to book there. https://first-rehab.com/page-sitemap.xml and https://www.google.com/maps/search/First+Rehab+404+Main+St+Spotswood+NJ
